analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. Per the complete range map, the only changed line is head line 671 in docs/architecture/inference.md, a new scheduler-table row on prompt-chunk attention. It documents 128-query blocks via DARKBLOOM_CBV2_ATTN_QUERY_BLOCK and a fused `.causal` MLX call for eligible full-attention chunks. Eligibility requires no window, softcap, vision span or bidirectional mask, and a fusable head_dim. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 restores blocked attention.

This describes a performance and numeric execution path inside TB-007, the in-process MLX engine. It does not change encryption (T-008), cache scoping or at-rest storage (T-041/SEC-035), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), authorization or billing.

The documented eligibility exclusions (vision, bidirectional, windowed) keep masking semantics intact for non-causal cases. Any correctness risk, such as the fused causal mask diverging from the absolute mask on paged KV, would be an output-integrity concern near T-007. That cannot be evaluated from documentation; the referenced sources AttentionV1.swift (`usesFusedCausalPrefill`) and PagedLayerCache.swift (`prefillAttend`) are not supplied.

The new env vars are performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* keys. Head line 726 states that unrecognized or performance-affecting keys are rejected for deadline qualification; whether these new keys are covered by that guard is unverified, and it is not a security control anyway.

The remaining text in both units (Nemotron Super slot, prefix bank scoped by authenticated cache scope at lines 159-166 and 360-362, and deadlines) is unchanged context. No regression was identified.
